aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: When Nobita and his friends embark on an undersea summer camping trip, they discover an ancient underwater civilization and must unite to stop an automated apocalyptic defense system from destroying the world.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Seeking an exciting location for summer vacation, Doraemon takes Nobita and his friends on a deep-sea camping expedition using futuristic gadgets like the Adapt-Ray and an AI-powered Underwater Buggy. During their journey along the ocean floor, they encounter a member of the hidden underwater kingdom of Mu and learn of an impending global crisis. An ancient automated fortress called the Castle of the Undersea Devil, controlled by the rogue computer system Poseidon, has reawakened and threatens to unleash apocalyptic weapons. Together with their new aquatic allies, the group sets out on a perilous mission into the oceanic depths to disarm the fortress and save both land and sea.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Debating where to spend their summer vacation, Nobita and his friends decide to go underwater camping using Doraemon's gadgets, including the Adapt-Ray that allows them to breathe and move freely under the ocean. Accompanied by their sentient transport vehicle, the Underwater Buggy, the group explores breathtaking marine environments and uncovers mysterious sunken ships. Their adventure takes a serious turn when Suneo and Gian stray into the Bermuda Triangle, leading to their rescue by El, a young resident of the hidden undersea nation known as the Mu Federation. Upon being brought to Mu, the surface children learn that the underwater civilization distrusts humans, but everyone soon faces a mutual catastrophic threat. An ancient rival kingdom, Atlantis, lies in ruins, but its automated defense hub—the Castle of the Undersea Devil—remains active under the control of Poseidon, an unyielding artificial intelligence. Mistaking volcanic activity for an enemy surface assault, Poseidon prepares to launch apocalyptic nuclear missiles that will obliterate all life on Earth. Realizing the danger, Nobita, Doraemon, and their companions volunteer to infiltrate the forbidden Atlantic territory to shut down the rogue supercomputer. Facing relentless robotic guardians and tight deadlines, the friends rely on courage, teamwork, and a noble sacrifice from their loyal Underwater Buggy to defeat Poseidon, ultimately saving the planet and bridging the gap between land and sea.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: While arguing over where to spend their summer break, Nobita and his friends accept Doraemon's idea for a thrilling deep-sea camping trip. Equipped with futuristic gadgets like the Adapt-Ray—which allows them to breathe underwater—and a talkative AI-powered Buggy, the five friends dive into the vast depths of the ocean. What starts as a fun vacation filled with deep-sea exploration and marine discoveries soon takes a dramatic turn when they uncover secret underwater civilizations that have remained hidden from humanity for centuries. Upon forming a tentative alliance with El, a citizen of the oceanic kingdom of Mu, the kids learn of an ancient automated stronghold known as the Castle of the Undersea Devil. When this forgotten fortress's rogue defense system reawakens and threatens global devastation, Nobita and his friends must muster all their courage, trust, and ingenuity to stop the catastrophe and preserve life across the world's oceans and continents.

story_structure.climax: In the heart of the enemy fortress, when all hope seems lost and Doraemon's group is overwhelmed, an unexpected sacrifice from a loyal ally breaches the main computer, triggering the collapse of the central threat.
story_structure.conflict: The group discovers the existence of the hidden, ancient undersea kingdom of Mu, but tensions rise when they realize a rogue automated military fortress, Atlantis, threatens to destroy the entire surface world.
story_structure.resolution: With the world saved and peace restored between the land and the ocean, the friends bid farewell to their undersea allies and return safely home to their everyday lives.
story_structure.introduction: Nobita and his friends decide to go on a summer camping trip to the deep ocean floor using Doraemon's gadgets, discovering a vibrant underwater world and an automated underwater buggy.
story_structure.risingAction: As the surface world faces imminent destruction from Atlantis's activated superweapons, the group allies with the people of Mu and embarks on a dangerous infiltration mission into the enemy territory to disarm the fortress.

faq.answer: It is a modern remake of the 1983 classic anime film, Doraemon: Nobita and the Castle of the Undersea Devil.
faq.question: Is this film an original story or a remake?

faq.answer: The dominant genres are Animated, Sci-Fi Fantasy, and Underwater Adventure, combined with family comedy.
faq.question: What is the dominant genre of the movie?

faq.answer: Yes, like most Doraemon feature films, it includes an end-credits sequence followed by a short teaser clip previewing the next annual movie installment.
faq.question: Is there a post-credit scene in the movie?

faq.answer: The main cast includes Doraemon, Nobita, Shizuka, Gian, and Suneo, along with special adventure companions like El from the Mu Federation and the sentient Underwater Buggy.
faq.question: Who are the main characters featured in the story?

faq.answer: The film explores themes of deep friendship, courage, teamwork, environmental wonder, and overcoming prejudice between different civilizations.
faq.question: What primary themes does the movie explore?

faq.answer: It is designed as a family-friendly film suitable for children, anime fans, and nostalgic adult audiences who grew up with the Doraemon series.
faq.question: What target audience is this movie intended for?

faq.answer: Key gadgets include the Adaptation Ray (Tekio Light), which allows the characters to breathe and live underwater, and the sentient Underwater Buggy.
faq.question: What iconic Doraemon gadgets play a major role in the plot?

faq.answer: The film was produced by Shin-Ei Animation, distributed by Toho, and directed by Tetsuo Yajima.
